evals.prompt: Build a 3-year commercial projection for a new internal developer platform that we expect 800 engineers to use. Initial build cost is roughly $1.2M, ongoing run cost $400k/year.
evals.description: Standard internal platform business case with concrete numbers.
expected_output_criteria: Quantifies productivity savings per engineer with explicit assumption (e.g., hours saved per week, fully loaded engineer cost)
Produces 3-year financial table covering investment, run cost, hard savings, soft savings, and net benefit
States a clear payback period in months and a 3-year ROI percentage
Lists 3+ named assumptions that drive the result and flags which are most sensitive
Includes a one-paragraph executive summary suitable for a leadership steering committee

evals.prompt: Justify replacing our in-house CI runner fleet with a managed SaaS that costs $480k/year. Current self-hosted cost is opaque - we don't know it. What's the business case?
evals.description: Medium scenario where the user lacks a baseline cost and the skill must reason about uncertainty.
expected_output_criteria: Explicitly flags missing baseline as a critical gap and proposes how to estimate it (cloud bill share, SRE hours, hardware amortisation)
Builds a high/expected/low scenario range rather than a single point estimate
Separates hard savings (cost replacement) from soft savings (faster CI, fewer flakes) with distinct confidence levels
Identifies switching cost, migration risk, and lock-in as quantified line items, not generic disclaimers
Recommends a decision (proceed / pilot / reject) tied to a specific threshold in the model

evals.prompt: We pitched a $4M data platform to the CFO and she said the soft-savings number was 'a fantasy'. Help me defend or rework the case.
evals.description: Hard case requiring quantification rigour and pushback handling.
expected_output_criteria: Re-derives soft savings from first principles with named comparable benchmarks or internal evidence
Distinguishes between hard, semi-hard, and soft benefit categories with separate confidence levels
Proposes a phased commit (Phase 1 funded only against hard savings) so the case can stand without the disputed soft number
Names specific risks the CFO is likely concerned about (double-counting, optimistic adoption, unmeasured opportunity cost) and addresses each
Produces a revised 1-page brief framed as a response, not a re-pitch
